report.source_text: The patient’s visual acuity consisted of light perception in the right eye and 3-m finger count in the left eye. Pupils of both eyes were midsize and briskly reactive, and no relative afferent pupillary defect was detected. Intraocular pressure (IOP) of both eyes were within normal limits. Conjunctiva and sclera were white and quiet. Cornea was clear. Anterior chamber was deep and quiet, the lenses were clear, and no vitreous hemorrhage was detected. Overall, anterior segment examination was unremarkable. Dilated fundus examination was performed. As shown in Fig. 2, in the right eye subhyaloid hemorrhage along with peripapillary intraretinal and flame-shaped hemorrhages were observed. Subhyaloid and intraretinal hemorrhages, along with a yellowish dense exudate in the fovea, is apparent in the fundus image of the left eye, as shown in Fig. 3.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old male with acute monocytic leukemia in remission presented with fever, headache, blurred vision, pallor, petechiae, and gum bleeding. Fundoscopic examination revealed subhyaloid hemorrhage, intraretinal and flame-shaped hemorrhages, and foveal exudate consistent with leukemic retinopathy. Brain CT showed left frontal and parietal subarachnoid hemorrhage. These hemorrhagic manifestations combined with the clinical presentation and history of AML support the diagnosis of leukemic retinopathy likely due to underlying pancytopenia.
